analysis.title: Ruminations Macro Micro Markets 5 Oct 2026
key_insights: Headline equity indices at record highs while sentiment, volatility and cross-asset signals look stressed. Traditional correlations are broken: equities vs yields, index vol vs single-stock/theme/factor vol, equity levels vs gross, var vs gross, rates vol vs equity vol.
The week's dovish trifecta of soft jobs, tame PCE and the G7 oil release shifted odds toward a Fed pause and eventual easing, which supports long-duration growth, real assets and hard money.

Beneath the index highs: homebuilders are down 15-20% in the last month, semis vs software are see-sawing, real assets and high-ROIC vs duration are whipsawed, and shorts and crowding are harder to manage. Consumer inertia is the latest area under AI disruption pressure, and euro banks are caught in euro sovereign concerns.

Market leadership is narrow: Meta has risen sharply in recent weeks, Nvidia hit an all-time high Friday and is approaching $6 trillion market cap, and Microsoft is up 50% from its July lows and positive on the year.
Equities are less linked to macro than usual. As long as belief in AI and AI capex holds, oil, rate policy, deficits, jobs, yields and geopolitics are secondary in the market's weighing.
The three main pillars to watch are yields/rates, oil and the AI theme. October is a heavy news month with Treasury auctions, earnings, elections and geopolitics.

Flows are producing binary, two-sided moves (all selling with no buyers, or all buying with no supply), seen in JGBs, OATs, global front-end rates, Mag7 ETFs, gold and Hynix/Korea. Retail and institutional flows appear increasingly correlated, adding velocity.

Politics is polarizing: social unrest in Spain, French budget negotiations, UK budget, Brazil's Bolsonaro vs Lula, and the US midterms. Molavi sees a risk of violent policy swings between ideologies and politicisation of data centres and AI.

Geopolitics: troop increases in Iran, return of terrorism, Russia/Ukraine ongoing, and a US/Xi summit as the big game. Molavi frames a fragmented 'Cold War 2' where tariffs and technology are linked, with second-order allegiances such as China buying energy from Russia/Iran.

Yields: the US 30-year is around 6.25%, the highest since 2002, and the UK 30-year is around 6.25%, the highest since 1998, with US 10-year and 30-year rising despite a Fed hike. France just had its worst bond quarter since the creation of the euro.

France: the CAC is one of the only global markets down on the year, and the OAT market is under stress with de-risking flows. The ECB is constrained politically and legally, and France may fall outside the TPI backstop given spring 2027 elections.

Southern Europe is attracting foreign investment (Solaria and PPC hyperscaler deals) and talent, with political and fiscal stability. Caution: higher yields hurt real estate, and house prices in Greece, Spain and Portugal are up materially with GDP highly correlated to real estate.

AI capex historical analogy: railways 1845, utilities 1929, Japan 1989, dotcom 2000 and shale 2014 all ended on a central bank pivot, in the order stocks peak, capex keeps rising for 6-24 months, capex rolls, then stocks roll.

Concentration in one theme as a share of S&P market cap: railroads 1830s 63%, utilities 1920s 36%, Nifty Fifty 1972 40%, Japan 1985 44%, TMT 1999 41%, AI big 10 now 42% and possibly higher with one or two new IPOs.

Issuance is showing strain: secondary sell-downs have performed poorly globally and US IPOs have been paused. Investors are more discerning than in H1. A bearish read points to slowing retail momentum and a bid-offer gap between public and private market marks.

Mixed signals: S&P and Nasdaq are at record highs while the job market is at a 10-year low on a blend of hiring, quits, openings, hours, wages, temp jobs, claims, Sahm rule and postings. The market is a narrow proxy for about 10 of the top 50 stocks tied to AI, not the economy.

Speed of value creation: Anthropic went from zero to about $2 trillion in 5 years, and some AI firms reached $500m+ ARR in about a year (Lovable, Cursor). In venture, Ineffable Intelligence was priced at $55m by Sequoia and about a month later at $4bn and $5.1bn by Index and Lightspeed in the same round.
Data centre deployment likely caps at around 20-25 GW by early next year due to delays, politics and bottlenecks. Pre-AI, only 72% of data centre builds came online on time.
Closing analogy: annual photographs rose from a few thousand in 1840 to 2 trillion this year despite casualties such as Polaroid, arguing that change is constant.

tension_points.bull_case: Record S&P and Nasdaq levels, Nvidia near $6 trillion, Microsoft up 50% from July lows, and a dovish week shifting odds toward a Fed pause and easing support long-duration growth.
tension_points.bear_case: Concentration in the AI big 10 is 42% of the S&P, the job market is at a 10-year low, yields are at multi-decade highs, IPOs are pausing, and past capex cycles ended with a central bank pivot.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A central bank pivot, or a roll-over in AI capex, which historically precedes stocks rolling.

tension_points.bull_case: Belief in AI and AI capex keeps macro factors secondary, and demand for compute drives data centre build-out.
tension_points.bear_case: In past cycles stocks peaked first, then capex kept rising for 6-24 months before rolling, and data centre deployment caps at 20-25 GW due to bottlenecks.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Capex roll-over following a central bank pivot.

tension_points.bull_case: The pause reflects healthy price discipline.
tension_points.bear_case: The pause reflects slowing retail momentum and a public-private bid-offer gap, with a wider discount demanded for new issues.
